fields.acceptance: Go tests in internal/api (go test -trimpath ./internal/api -run 'RecordAgentActor') assert: recording the actor of a session whose actor an in-flight change set (another run's branch merged in) already recorded with the same session value writes no new node and returns that actor; a landed or in-flight actor holding claude-code-0123abcd under another session value is not returned, and the new actor gets a unique handle, so no two actors hold one handle; rhiza check on the result reports no duplicate handle.
fields.statement: Recording an agent actor for a session reuses the actor that a landed or in-flight change set already recorded for that session (its session field equals the session ID) instead of writing a second node, so review's code check no longer fails on a duplicate actor handle. Session IDs are UUIDv7, so sessions launched close together share the base handle <agent>-<first 8 hex>: an actor of another session holding that handle, landed or in flight, is never reused, and the new actor gets a unique handle of its own.
